name: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)
hardware: SPICE flow-duct hardware in Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG); 89 test points
fuel: 41 samples: thin flat (SIBAL cotton-fiberglass, Nomex, Ultem), thick flat (PMMA, wax-saturated fiberglass), PMMA spheres (1 and 2 cm), candles in ceramic tubes (paraffin, Japan wax)
measures: Video, radiometer (flame output), anemometer; flame shape, spread rate, time to extinction vs N2 flow (0-500 cc/min)
objective: Tests whether materials burn as well or better in microgravity than in 1g, and how nitrogen suppression works. Guides extinguishing strategies and heat-release models.
details: Finding for design: the best point to apply suppressant is not obvious in microgravity, and a suppressant stream can even make a flame worse by entraining oxygen. Current NASA material screening (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) is based on 1g behaviour.

name: BASS-II
fuel: 100 samples: acrylic films/sheets, SIBAL fabric, black/clear acrylic rods, section of a large acrylic sphere
o2: Varied ambient oxygen (nitrogen vitiation up to 500 cc/min)
measures: Radiometer, video; spread rate, flame length, extinction limits, heat release rate, combustion completeness, equivalence ratio
objective: Find the worst-case flammability in spacecraft conditions vs the 1g upward-burning test; minimum oxygen and flow where materials burn.
details: Results: thin and thick fuel spread rates measured plus a thin-to-thick transition formula. Models predict higher spread rates than observed, so they need improvement. Results will guide material choice for future spacecraft.

name: Saffire-I, -II, -III
objective: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration at scale beyond lab tests. Check if full data is in PSI.

name: SAME / SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment)
fuel: Smoke from heated Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose (SAME-R: also cotton, Pyrell) and dibutyl-phthalate on a wick; 30 samples in SAME
airflow: Varied airflow, heating temperature and smoke aging time
measures: Particle size distribution; number, diameter and mass concentration; TEM images; ISS photoelectric and Shuttle ionization detectors
objective: Measure smoke particle sizes in microgravity and test how well ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors work.
details: Findings: all samples produced many sub-micron particles that ionization detectors catch best, but light-scattering detectors also work well for most cases. Pre-fire overheating can create wider size distributions, so detectors that measure a wide size range may be more reliable. Future detectors should target pre-fire pyrolysis products, not just soot.

name: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)
hardware: Same instrument as SAME, used for dust
objective: Shows the smoke detector can tell dust from smoke, reducing false alarms.

name: FLEX / FLEX-2 (Flame Extinguishment Experiment)
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
fuel: Methanol and heptane droplets, 2-5 mm (FLEX-2: 2-4 mm; fuel mixtures, droplet pairs, convective flow, 30-60 tests per group)
o2: Oxygen mole fraction 0.10 to 0.50; CO2 or helium suppressant up to about 0.70
measures: Droplet burning rate, extinction, flame radiation, soot concentration and temperature; pressure 0.5-1.0 atm
objective: Quantify how well inert gases suppress flames and find the limiting oxygen index across candidate cabin pressures and oxygen levels.
details: Low pressure data (0.5 atm) supports the strategy of venting a cabin to space to put out a fire.

name: CFI (Cool Flames Investigation)
objective: Study low-temperature cool flames. Less direct for fire safety.

name: ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)
fuel: Gaseous fuel (e.g. propane) from a porous spherical burner
measures: Quasi-steady spherical cool diffusion flame structure and extinction
objective: First steady spherical cool diffusion flames; challenge text says tests reached up to 85% oxygen.
source: NASA ACME fact sheet and challenge text

name: ACME BRE (Burning Rate Emulator)
hardware: ACME modular hardware in CIR (about 90 L chamber)
fuel: Flat porous burner fed gaseous fuel, emulating paper, plastic and alcohol burning
measures: Surface temperature, burner heat flux (2 heat flux transducers), flow rate, video
objective: Fire prevention: ignition and extinction behaviour, and whether existing flammability tests are valid in low and partial gravity.

name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
hardware: ACME in CIR; electrode mesh up to +/-10 kV at 35 or 50 mm
measures: Ion current through the flame, flame response time to electric forcing
objective: How electric fields change flame shape and limits. Listed in this challenge as a partial-gravity proxy.

name: SPICE (Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment)
objective: How much soot/smoke flames make, which feeds detection design.

name: SLICE (Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)
objective: Flame stability and liftoff. Useful for models, indirect for safety.

name: BASS-M (Burning and Suppression of Solids-Milliken)
fuel: 44 cotton textile samples, 11 textile types incl. 10 flame-retardant treated
measures: Radiometer, video; self-extinguishing ability, time to extinction
objective: How low gravity changes the behaviour of flame-retardant textiles compared with the terrestrial upward-burning test.
details: Flame-retardant textiles are used in spacecraft and on Earth, so results help both material testing procedures and materials science.

name: ACME CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)
fuel: Methane and ethylene in air coflow
airflow: Varied injection velocity and fuel dilution
measures: Flame structure, temperature, soot volume fraction (color imaging, pyrometry, extinction)
objective: Sooty flames and highly diluted near-extinction flames, for chemical kinetics and soot models.
details: Microgravity flames contain 5 to 8 times more soot than equivalent 1g flames, and highly diluted flames are more stable than in 1g, extending dilution limits.
